_note: What the walkman caught at the bedside (tape-record R2), Claude's. One night per day's god, nights 5–17; the last line is what reversed play brings out. Night 11 is absent on purpose: its recording is day 12's own file 梦话_1026.m4a (files.json a-sleeptalk), which the lock reads. Day N is 2028-10-(15+N).

5.name: sleeptalk_1020.m4a
lines: "...Vivi, can you hear me over there..."
Played backwards: "...I can hear. Even in the jar I can hear."

6.name: sleeptalk_1021.m4a
lines: Played backwards: "...painted from a photo. The photo is yours."

7.name: sleeptalk_1022.m4a
lines: "...meeting closed... it's closed... why are you all still here..."
Played backwards: "...you never gave me licence to depart."

8.name: sleeptalk_1023.m4a
lines: "...King, nine till noon... Duke... what time is Duke..."
Played backwards: "...we're always free. It's you lot who aren't."

9.name: sleeptalk_1024.m4a
lines: "...guest of honour in the triangle... not in the circle..."
"...who printed the script... why is it yellow..."
Played backwards: "...Act Two. See you tomorrow."

10.name: sleeptalk_1025.m4a
lines: "...one word at a time... never a whole line..."
"...Carcosa... how do you say this one..."
Played backwards: "...you read it. The whole line."

12.name: sleeptalk_1027.m4a
lines: (Turning over, three hundred and twelve times.)
Played backwards: "...nobody sleeps this week. You included."

13.name: sleeptalk_1028.m4a
lines: "...the key... and the gate... and the guardian..."
Played backwards: "...the gate is under your pillow."

15.name: sleeptalk_1030.m4a
lines: "...thank you to our speaker... meeting closed..."
"...why are you sitting on the desk..."
Played backwards: "...one of the audience is you."

16.name: sleeptalk_1031.m4a
lines: (A flute. Always the same. Not fast, not slow.)
Played backwards: (the flute. Backwards it's the same.)

17.name: sleeptalk_1101.m4a
lines: Played backwards: "...did you say that, or did I."
